On March 31, 2026, a rather odd complaint arrived at the Bucks County, Pennsylvania District Attorney’s Office. It came from the local sheriff’s office, and it concerned one of their own, Deputy Sheriff Ryan Gaffney. The allegation was unusual: Gaffney had used his iPhone to snap photos of nude prisoners he had encountered in his job—and he had then shared those photos with “several female civilian employees inside the Sheriff’s Office.” The main claim involved a local man suffering a mental health crisis on the morning of January 30, 2026. Five fully uniformed deputies had arrived at the house and were in the upstairs bedroom. Their detainee was naked from the waist down and had just been persuaded to put on some pants.

At some point in this process, Gaffney was believed to have obtained a photo of the man’s genitalia, because after the arrest and booking, another deputy admitted that he had seen Gaffney showing the photo on his phone to a female civilian employee “in jest.” This same witness said that Gaffney had done something similar in late 2024, taking a photo of a “subject’s naked buttocks while in custody.” Investigators checked the logs from the Axon system. These showed that Gaffney did not access bodycam footage from the January incident for many months. So if Gaffney had shown a photo on his phone to the female employee on the day of the arrest, it must have come from some other source.

Perhaps Gaffney had used his own phone? Yet his bodycam footage never showed it. Still, it did show him covering his bodycam’s lens with a hand for a few moments. Investigators pulled bodycam footage from other cops who had been in the room. These picked up Gaffney as the deputies stood around the bed of the nude man. According to investigators, when the man sat down on the bed to pull on his pants, Gaffney removed a glove from his right hand and pulled an iPhone 15 from his right pants pocket. He was then “observed manipulating the cell phone in his right hand” and putting it back in his pocket.

On March 31, 2026, a rather odd complaint arrived at the Bucks County, Pennsylvania District Attorney’s Office.

It came from the local sheriff’s office, and it concerned one of their own, Deputy Sheriff Ryan Gaffney. The allegation was unusual: Gaffney had used his iPhone to snap photos of nude prisoners he had encountered in his job—and he had then shared those photos with “several female civilian employees inside the Sheriff’s Office.”

The main claim involved a local man suffering a mental health crisis on the morning of January 30, 2026. Five fully uniformed deputies had arrived at the house and were in the upstairs bedroom. Their detainee was naked from the waist down and had just been persuaded to put on some pants.

At some point in this process, Gaffney was believed to have obtained a photo of the man’s genitalia, because after the arrest and booking, another deputy admitted that he had seen Gaffney showing the photo on his phone to a female civilian employee “in jest.” This same witness said that Gaffney had done something similar in late 2024, taking a photo of a “subject’s naked buttocks while in custody.”

Investigators checked the logs from the Axon system. These showed that Gaffney did not access bodycam footage from the January incident for many months. So if Gaffney had shown a photo on his phone to the female employee on the day of the arrest, it must have come from some other source.

Perhaps Gaffney had used his own phone? Yet his bodycam footage never showed it. Still, it did show him covering his bodycam’s lens with a hand for a few moments.

Investigators pulled bodycam footage from other cops who had been in the room. These picked up Gaffney as the deputies stood around the bed of the nude man. According to investigators, when the man sat down on the bed to pull on his pants, Gaffney removed a glove from his right hand and pulled an iPhone 15 from his right pants pocket. He was then “observed manipulating the cell phone in his right hand” and putting it back in his pocket.

Investigators say that he placed his left hand over his bodycam, blocking its view, as he reached into his pocket again to retrieve the cell phone. He pointed it for just a moment toward the man getting dressed while the phone screen appeared to have “the camera application open,” investigators say.

This gave them enough to go to a judge. On April 22, they obtained a warrant to search Gaffney’s cell phone, which was done the next day by a detective unaffiliated

payload.title: Apulaissheriffin epäillään kuvanneen alastonta kiinniotettua – puhelimen käyttö tallentui muiden vartalokameroihin
payload.summary: Pennsylvanialaisen apulaissheriffin epäillään kuvanneen puolialastonta kiinniotettua omalla iPhonellaan. Hänen vartalokameransa linssi peittyi hetkeksi, mutta muiden paikalla olleiden viranomaisten tallenteet näyttivät hänen käsittelevän puhelinta miehen vierellä.
payload.content:
Pennsylvanian Bucks Countyn apulaissheriffi Ryan Gaffneyta epäillään alastomien kiinniotettujen kuvaamisesta omalla iPhonellaan ja kuvien näyttämisestä sheriffinviraston siviilityöntekijöille. Tammikuun 2026 tapahtumassa hänen oman vartalokameransa linssi peittyi hetkeksi, mutta muiden huoneessa olleiden apulaissheriffien tallenteet näyttivät hänen ottavan puhelimen esiin puolialastoman miehen vierellä ja käsittelevän sitä kädessään.

## Ilmoitus johti tutkintaan

Bucks Countyn syyttäjänvirasto sai 31. maaliskuuta 2026 paikalliselta sheriffinvirastolta ilmoituksen, joka koski sen omaa työntekijää Gaffneyta. Ilmoituksen mukaan hän oli käyttänyt iPhoneaan työssään kohtaamiensa alastomien kiinniotettujen kuvaamiseen ja näyttänyt kuvia useille sheriffinvirastossa työskenteleville naispuolisille siviilityöntekijöille.

Keskeinen epäily liittyy 30. tammikuuta 2026 sattuneeseen tilanteeseen. Viisi täysin virkapukuista apulaissheriffiä oli saapunut mielenterveyskriisistä kärsineen paikallisen miehen kotiin ja kokoontunut yläkerran makuuhuoneeseen. Mies oli alasti vyötäröstä alaspäin, ja viranomaiset olivat juuri saaneet hänet suostuteltua pukemaan housut.

Kiinnioton ja säilöön kirjaamisen jälkeen toinen apulaissheriffi kertoi nähneensä Gaffneyn näyttävän puhelimestaan naispuoliselle siviilityöntekijälle kuvaa, jonka uskottiin esittävän miehen sukuelimiä. Todistajan mukaan kuvaa näytettiin pilailumielessä. Sama todistaja kertoi Gaffneyn toimineen samankaltaisesti loppuvuonna 2024, jolloin tämä oli kuvannut säilössä olleen henkilön paljasta takapuolta.

## Tallenteita verrattiin keskenään

Tutkijat tarkastivat vartalokameroiden Axon-järjestelmän käyttölokit. Niiden mukaan Gaffney ei avannut tammikuun tilanteen vartalokameratallenteita moneen kuukauteen. Jos hän siis näytti kuvan puhelimestaan jo kiinniottopäivänä, se ei tutkijoiden päätelmän mukaan voinut olla peräisin vasta myöhemmin katsotusta vartalokamera-aineistosta. Tämän vuoksi huomio kohdistui mahdollisuuteen, että kuva oli otettu Gaffneyn omalla puhelimella.

Gaffneyn oma vartalokameratallenne ei näyttänyt puhelimen esiin ottamista, mutta siinä hänen nähtiin peittävän kameran linssin kädellään muutamaksi hetkeksi. Muiden samassa huoneessa olleiden apulaissheriffien tallenteissa Gaffney näkyi sängyn vierellä, kun mies istuutui vetämään housuja jalkaansa. Tutkijoiden mukaan Gaffney riisui oikean käden käsineensä, otti oikeasta housuntaskustaan iPhone 15:n, käsitteli puhelinta oikeassa kädessään ja pani sen takaisin taskuun. Lähdeaineisto ei kerro Gaffneyn vastauksesta epäilyihin eikä yksilöi mahdollisia syytteitä.
summary_bullets: Ryan Gaffneyta epäillään alastomien kiinniotettujen kuvaamisesta omalla puhelimellaan.
Hänen vartalokameransa linssi peittyi hetkeksi tammikuussa tapahtuneen kiinnioton aikana.
Muiden apulaissheriffien kamerat tallensivat Gaffneyn ottavan iPhone 15 -puhelimen esiin kiinniotetun vierellä.
payload.journalist_note: Epäilyt, todistajan kertomukset ja tutkijoiden tallenteista tekemät havainnot on erotettu toisistaan. Muiden vartalokameroiden tallenteet näyttävät puhelimen käsittelyn, mutta lähdeaineisto ei kerro niiden tallentaneen itse valokuvan ottamista.

At some point in this process, Gaffney was believed to have obtained a photo of the man’s genitalia, because after the arrest and booking, another deputy admitted that he had seen Gaffney showing the photo on his phone to a female civilian employee “in jest.” This same witness said that Gaffney had done something similar in late 2024, taking a photo of a “subject’s naked buttocks while in custody.” Investigators checked the logs from the Axon system. These showed that Gaffney did not access bodycam footage from the January incident for many months. So if Gaffney had shown a photo on his phone to the female employee on the day of the arrest, it must have come from some other source.

Perhaps Gaffney had used his own phone? Yet his bodycam footage never showed it. Still, it did show him covering his bodycam’s lens with a hand for a few moments. Investigators pulled bodycam footage from other cops who had been in the room. These picked up Gaffney as the deputies stood around the bed of the nude man. According to investigators, when the man sat down on the bed to pull on his pants, Gaffney removed a glove from his right hand and pulled an iPhone 15 from his right pants pocket. He was then “observed manipulating the cell phone in his right hand” and putting it back in his pocket.
